facts.statement: Desmatosuchus is an extinct genus of archosaur belonging to the order Aetosauria.
facts.quote: taxon: Desmatosuchus

facts.statement: The genus Desmatosuchus was first described by Case in 1920.
facts.quote: authority: Case, 1920

facts.statement: Desmatosuchus lived during the Late Triassic, specifically from the Carnian to the Norian stages.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Triassic (Carnian to Norian)

facts.statement: Fossils of Desmatosuchus have been found in North America and potentially in India during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: It lived in North America and potentially India during the Late Triassic.

facts.statement: Desmatosuchus was a large quadrupedal reptile that measured between 4.5 and over 5 meters in length and weighed approximately 280 to 300 kilograms.
facts.quote: Desmatosuchus was a large quadrupedal reptile measuring 4.5 m to over 5 m long and weighing about 280 - 300 kg.

facts.statement: Desmatosuchus possessed large acromion processes on its scapulae, commonly referred to as shoulder spikes.
facts.quote: Its scapulae which possessed large acromion processes commonly referred to as "shoulder spikes".

facts.statement: Desmatosuchus is unique among aetosaurs because its species are the only known ones to lack teeth on their premaxillae.
facts.quote: Desmatosuchus is unique among aetosaurs in that its species are the only known aetosaurs that lacked teeth on their premaxillae.

facts.statement: The lateral scutes of Desmatosuchus had well-developed spine-like processes that pointed out laterally and dorso-posteriorly.
facts.quote: The lateral scutes had well-developed spine-like processes which pointed out laterally and dorso-posteriorly.

facts.statement: The front spine on Desmatosuchus was much larger, measuring around 28 centimeters in length, and was recurved.
facts.quote: The front spine was much larger, around 28 centimeters long, and was recurved.

facts.statement: Two species are currently accepted as valid for Desmatosuchus: D. spurensis and D. smalli, the latter named after Brian J. Small.
facts.quote: Two species were accepted as valid: D. spurensis and D. smalli, named after Brian J. Small for his contribution to the study of this genus.

facts.statement: Desmatosuchus likely fed by digging up soft vegetation, indicated by its shovel-like snout and blunt teeth.
facts.quote: This, combined with its shovel like snout, indicate that Desmatosuchus fed by digging up soft vegetation.

facts.statement: The armor and spikes were the only means of defense Desmatosuchus had against predators.
facts.quote: The armor and spikes of Desmatosuchus were its only ways to defend itself from predators.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence shows that Postosuchus preyed on Desmatosuchus, as Desmatosuchus bones have been found among Postosuchus skeletons.
facts.quote: Several Desmatosuchus bones have been found amongst skeletons of Postosuchus, indicating predation by Postosuchus.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Desmatosuchus may have been omnivorous or even an insectivore, though the general consensus remains that it was herbivorous.
facts.quote: It has also been suggested that Desmatosuchus could have been omnivorous or even an insectivore.

facts.statement: Variation in the size of the second most anterior spike may indicate sexual dimorphism or serve as a form of sexual display.
facts.quote: This variation may indicate sexual dimorphism. It has also been hypothesized as a form of sexual display.

facts.statement: Desmatosuchus lived during the Triassic period in Texas.
facts.quote: Vivió durante en el período Triásico en Texas.

facts.statement: Desmatosuchus had an armored body and a head that vaguely resembled a pig.
facts.quote: Desmatosuchus era parecido a sus parientes, con un cuerpo acorazado y una cabeza que recuerda vagamente a la de un cerdo.

facts.statement: It possessed a shovel-shaped snout and weak teeth, suggesting it fed by pulling off soft plants.
facts.quote: Tenía un hocico en forma de pala y dientes débiles que sugieren que se alimentaba arrancando plantas suaves.

facts.statement: Like many relatives, it had bony plates covering its back, tail, and parts of its lower body.
facts.quote: Como muchos de sus parientes, tenía placas óseas cubriendo su espalda, cola y partes de su zona baja.

facts.statement: Unlike other aetosaurs, Desmatosuchus had two rows of spines running along the sides of its back.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, a diferencia de los demás aetosaurios Desmatosuchus también tenía dos filas de espinas a lo largo de los lados de su espalda.

facts.statement: The largest spines, located over the shoulders, measured 45 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Las mayores espinas, situadas sobre los hombros, medían 45 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: These spines likely provided additional protection against predators.
facts.quote: Estas probablemente le daban protección adicional contra los depredadores.

facts.statement: Three species are considered valid: D. haplocerus, D. spurensis, and D. smalli.
facts.quote: Tres especies son consideradas válidas: D. haplocerus, D. spurensis y D. smalli.

facts.statement: D. chamaensis is considered a distinct genus, but there is controversy regarding whether it should be referred to the genera Heliocanthus or Rioarribasuchus.
facts.quote: Desmatosuchus chamaensis es considerado como un género distinto, pero existe una controversia acerca de si se podría referir a los géneros Heliocanthus o Rioarribasuchus.

facts.statement: Its parent group is Desmatosuchini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Desmatosuchini

facts.statement: It belongs to the family Stagonolepididae.
facts.quote: Family: Stagonolepididae

facts.statement: It is classified as a reptile.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species is Desmatosuchus spurensis.
facts.quote: Type species: Desmatosuchus spurensis

facts.statement: It lived from the Carnian to the Norian stages, between 237 and 205.7 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Norian (237 to 205.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 14 recorded fossil occurrences of Desmatosuchus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 14

facts.statement: It was featured in the Discovery Channel documentary When Dinosaurs Roamed America, where it was shown driving away a Coelophysis and later the predator Rutiodon.
facts.quote: Desmatosuchus fue representado en el documental de Discovery Channel When Dinosaurs Roamed America, en el cual es mostrado alejando a un Coelophysis y más tarde al depredador Rutiodon.

facts.statement: It also appeared in an episode of the miniseries Animal Armageddon, where it was hunted by Staurikosaurus, one of the earliest dinosaurs, in a eventual extinction event.
facts.quote: Desmatosuchus también apareció en un capítulo de la miniserie Animal Armageddon, en la cual es cazado por Staurikosaurus, uno de los primeros dinosaurios, en una eventual extinción.
